title: Saviour, Thy Law We Love
description: Saviour, Thy Law We Love in Tonic Solfa to FRANCONIA, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: Lydia Sigourney wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 672 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Baptism”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Short Metre (6.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to FRANCONIA; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Sa-viour, thy law we love, Thy pure e-xam-ple bless, And with a firm, un-wa-vering zeal, Would in thy foot-steps press.

lines: And with a firm, unwavering zeal,
Not to the scourge, the thorn, the cross,

licence: Public domain: Lydia Sigourney died in 1865.
credits: Words by Lydia Sigourney (1791–1865), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to FRANCONIA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
